ai.definition: Space Exploration Milestones refer to key achievements made by various space agencies and private companies in the field of space exploration. These milestones include landing on celestial bodies, establishing orbiting stations, and conducting scientific research.
ai.howItWorks: These missions involve complex spacecraft designs that can withstand harsh interplanetary conditions. They utilize advanced propulsion systems, communication technologies, and remote sensing instruments to gather data about planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.
ai.problemSolved: Understanding the composition of celestial bodies, identifying potential resources (like water or minerals), and validating theories about planetary formation and evolution.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves creating highly specialized spacecraft components using advanced materials like carbon fiber composites and high-strength alloys. These components are then integrated into complex systems that must operate in extreme environments.
ai.buildProcess: Components are designed, fabricated, and tested to ensure they can withstand launch stresses and the harsh conditions of space. This includes thermal cycling tests, vacuum baking for electronics, and rigorous environmental testing.
ai.costDrivers: High material costs, specialized labor, and stringent quality control measures. Additionally, the cost of launches and maintaining spacecraft in orbit or on planetary surfaces are significant.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as more private companies enter the space exploration market, driving innovation and reducing costs through competition.
ai.regulation: Governed by international laws such as the Outer Space Treaty of 1967, with additional regulations from individual countries. These aim to ensure peaceful use and prevent contamination of celestial bodies.
ai.risks: Technological failures, launch risks, operational hazards in space, and potential legal disputes over resource claims.
ai.profitability: Currently not directly profitable but seen as a strategic investment for future economic benefits such as mining resources or establishing outposts.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include more frequent missions, longer-duration stays on other planets, and the development of in-situ resource utilization technologies.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking. Launch vehicles consume vast amounts of energy during ascent.

glossary.def: An international agreement signed in 1967 that prohibits any country from claiming sovereignty over outer space or celestial bodies.
The process of extracting and using resources found on other planets, moons, or asteroids for the benefit of space missions or future human settlements.

subsystems.name: Launch and interplanetary transfer
subsystems.role: gets the spacecraft off Earth and onto a path to its target.

subsystems.name: Entry, descent and landing
subsystems.role: survives the atmosphere and touches down in one piece, or deliberately impacts.

subsystems.name: Surface mobility
subsystems.role: carries instruments to rocks that are worth studying.
parts: solar arrays or radioisotope power source

subsystems.name: Sampling and return chain
subsystems.role: collects material and delivers it to Earth intact.

subsystems.name: Communications and navigation
subsystems.role: keeps the mission in contact across hundreds of millions of kilometres.

subsystems.name: In-situ resource utilisation
subsystems.role: makes consumables from local material instead of shipping them.

buildSteps.title: Choose a target and question
buildSteps.detail: A steering committee weighs scientific value against cost, launch window and landing risk.

buildSteps.title: Design and test the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Subsystems are built separately, then shaken, heated and cooled in vacuum chambers to survive launch and space.

buildSteps.title: Launch in a window
buildSteps.detail: Planetary alignments occur every couple of years, so missing the window means a long delay.

buildSteps.title: Cruise
buildSteps.detail: The craft coasts for months or years, with occasional trajectory corrections.

buildSteps.title: Land or orbit
buildSteps.detail: Entry, descent and landing is the riskiest phase; rover missions use cameras to compare the ground below with onboard maps and steer away from hazards.

buildSteps.title: Operate on the surface
buildSteps.detail: A ground team plans each sol of driving and instrument use, limited by how fast commands can travel.

buildSteps.title: Collect and seal samples
buildSteps.detail: Tubes of rock and soil are cached on the surface or loaded into an ascent vehicle.

buildSteps.title: Return and curate
buildSteps.detail: A capsule re-enters at high speed, is recovered, and the samples go into clean, catalogued storage for decades of later study.

prerequisites.why: mass and volume budgets decide which instruments and samples can fly.
every command and image depends on large ground antennas.
radio delay makes joystick flying impossible, so the craft must judge the last minute alone.
solar output falls off on dusty or distant worlds; radioisotope units are scarce and hard to make.
producing oxygen or water on another world is the difference between a visit and a base.
returned material must not contaminate Earth, and spacecraft must not contaminate the target.

pathway.milestone: robotic landers, rovers and sample returns — lunar material from Chang'e 5 and 6, asteroid material from Hayabusa2 and OSIRIS-REx
pathway.unlocks: ground-truth calibration of remote sensing and a curated scientific archive.

pathway.milestone: crewed lunar surface missions and a sustained orbital presence
pathway.unlocks: operating humans and hardware together beyond low Earth orbit.

pathway.milestone: Mars sample return and larger in-situ resource demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: laboratory-grade analysis of Martian rock and confidence in making fuel and oxygen locally.

pathway.milestone: outposts that live largely off local water ice and regolith
pathway.unlocks: long stays that do not depend on resupply from Earth.
